hook_structure: accusatory-callout hook stacked with word-by-word kinetic text: 'IF YOURE NOT MAKING VIDEOS because YOU DONT KNOW HOW TO EDIT' -> reframed as excuse ('EXCUSE = NO GOOD'), baiting viewer identity before pivoting to solution pitch

beats.card_text: IF YOURE NOT MAKING VIDEOS because
beats.read: Kinetic word-by-word caption build (NOT in red, VIDEOS in giant yellow) forces the eye to the accusation while speaker walks toward camera to build presence.

beats.card_text: YOU DONT KNOW HOW TO EDIT / EXCUSE = NO GOOD
beats.read: Continues the callout with DONT in red for emphasis then whip-crossfades into a big yellow EXCUSE card with red NO GOOD stamp, editorializing the audience's assumed objection before he even states it.

beats.card_text: and that's why / I started using / the Captions App.
beats.read: Location/lighting change (new room, natural window light) signals a new scene beat; word-level yellow captions keep pace with speech as he introduces the product with a floating app-icon graphic overlay.

beats.card_text: And trust me. / I get it. / I used to feel discouraged too when I didn't know how to edit.
beats.read: Hard cut to a static window-lit talking-head setup builds trust/rapport tone (no punch-ins), simple burned-in captions carry the sincerity beat without visual noise.

beats.cutaway_subject: Wide static shot of living room, speaker walking away from camera toward TV stand
beats.read: Rapid mechanical cuts (12.554/12.888/13.222) chain quick wide shots of him moving through the room, a physical scene transition bridging talking-head to phone-screen demo.

beats.cutaway_subject: Wide shot of him crouched by couch, back to camera, adjusting something
beats.read: Bare beat: no text or effect layered here, editor lets the silent physical action breathe as a bridge before the phone reveal.

beats.cutaway_subject: Screen-recording of Captions App UI: AI Edit button, Quick Trim upload, style browser, New Video settings, generating/loading chat
beats.card_text: With AI Edit / inside the Captions App / I just upload a raw clip / choose a style / then the Captions App / will edit everything for me in minutes.
beats.read: Green cutting-mat background frames every phone-screen recording like a tutorial insert; captions run continuously under the UI footage to narrate each tap as literal proof of the workflow.

beats.cutaway_subject: Close, shaky low-angle selfie shot of speaker reacting to phone screen
beats.card_text: and even if change a few things I still can.
beats.read: Jarring extreme close-up with visible motion blur mimics an offhand, unscripted 'caught in the moment' aside, contrasting the polished screen-record segment to feel authentic.

beats.cutaway_subject: Two large framed prints side-by-side: raw clip photo vs. finished 'EDITING' title-card photo, held up by speaker behind couch
beats.card_text: Now look at this / raw clip / compared to the / final version
beats.read: Physical before/after picture-frame prop is a tangible payoff device, letting the viewer visually compare raw vs. edited output rather than just being told about it.

beats.card_text: So if you wanna start posting videos creative journey
beats.read: Cut back to the original dim living-room set closes the loop visually to the opening scene, plain captions keep focus on the direct-address call to action.
App logo card floats in over speaker as final CTA beat, reinforcing brand recall right before the outro cut.

beats.cutaway_subject: TikTok loading/splash screen and profile search bar showing '@lucasxmoua'
beats.read: Native TikTok UI card is used as a platform-style outro/follow prompt, a deliberate bare-of-effects screen letting the app chrome itself do the closing CTA.
